parameters.content:
## Birthday & anniversary greetings on autopilot

Every morning at 08:00 this workflow reads your contact sheet, finds everyone
whose birthday or anniversary is **today**, renders a personal 1080×1920
greeting video for each of them with Zvid, optionally emails it, and writes the
year back so nobody is ever greeted twice.

The design is adapted from Zvid's celebration templates: serif name headline,
occasion pill, drifting bokeh lights, message card and brand sign-off.

### Setup (about five minutes)

1. **Zvid API key** — create one at https://app.zvid.io/api-keys
   Add an n8n **Header Auth** credential: name `x-api-key`, value = your key.
   Attach it to *Validate project (free)*, *Submit render* and
   *Get render status*.
2. **Google Sheets** — attach your Google credential to *Read contacts* and
   *Mark as sent*, then pick your spreadsheet + sheet in BOTH nodes.
   The expected columns are in the yellow note below.
3. **Open `Config`** — set `brandName`, your colours and the two default
   messages. Everything else has a working default.
4. **Run it.** *Validate project (free)* is free and runs first — it checks
   every payload and quotes the credit cost. The render then starts
   automatically, so **the first run spends credits** (~11 per greeting).
   Tip: put one test row with today's date in the sheet before you run.
5. Optional: set `sendEmail: true` and add an SMTP credential to
   *Send greeting email* (see the delivery note).

### Cost

A ~10 second greeting is about **11 Zvid credits**. Only days when someone
actually celebrates cost anything.

## Your contact sheet

One row per contact, with a header row:

| Name | Type | Date | Years | Email | LastSentYear | Message |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Maya Chen | birthday | 1994-07-27 | | maya@acme.com | | |
| Studio Nova | anniversary | 2016-03-02 | | hello@nova.io | 2025 | Ten amazing years! |

- **Type**: `birthday` or `anniversary` (anything else counts as birthday).
- **Date**: `YYYY-MM-DD` preferred. Only month + day decide the match; Feb 29
  contacts are greeted on Feb 28 in non-leap years.
- **Years** *(optional)*: shown as "Happy 10th …". Anniversaries auto-count
  from the Date's year; birthdays never do (never reveal an age uninvited —
  fill Years explicitly if you want "Happy 30th Birthday").
- **Email** *(optional)*: needed only when `sendEmail` is on.
- **LastSentYear**: managed by the workflow — leave it empty. Clear it to
  re-send someone this year.
- **Message** *(optional)*: overrides the default message for that contact.

Matching uses your **workflow timezone** (n8n Settings → Timezone).

## Make it yours (all in Config)

- `brandName`, `signoffText` — the footer mark and the "— The … Team" line.
- `accent` / `accent2` / `backgroundColor` / `textPrimary` / `textMuted` —
  the whole palette re-tints from these five values, including the gradients,
  bokeh lights and the delivery email.
- `headingFont` / `bodyFont` — any Google Font name.
- `birthdayMessage` / `anniversaryMessage` — `{name}`, `{years}` and
  `{brand}` are replaced per contact.
- `musicUrl` — any hosted mp3 under ~5 MB, or empty for a silent video.
- Long names and long messages auto-shrink to fit; nothing ever clips.

## Delivery & the sent-guard

`sendEmail` is **false** by default. Turn it on and attach any SMTP
credential to *Send greeting email* (set `emailFrom` in Config). Contacts
without an email address still get their video rendered — you can grab
`videoUrl` from the run output and deliver it any way you like (Slack,
WhatsApp, a CRM webhook…).

**Order matters:** the email is sent first, then `LastSentYear` is written.
A failed render or failed email stops the run *before* the write-back, so the
next run retries that contact — a greeting can be duplicated after a partial
failure, but never silently lost.

## Official Zvid nodes

These HTTP Request nodes are deliberately core-only so the workflow runs
anywhere, including n8n Cloud with nothing installed.

On self-hosted n8n you can install **`@zvid/n8n-nodes-zvid`**
(Settings → Community nodes) and swap them:

| HTTP Request node | Native replacement |
| --- | --- |
| Validate project (free) | **Zvid** → Render → Validate |
| Submit render | **Zvid** → Render → Create |
| Get render status + Wait | **Zvid Trigger** (render webhook) |

## ▶ Watch video

Click this node after a run: n8n renders the downloaded MP4 as an inline
video player with a download button — one greeting per contact, no URLs to
copy.

*Run summary* above still carries `videoUrl` (and `jobId`, `creditsCharged`)
if you want to pipe the result onward.
